dedupe_keys.name: address count listing files housing units and group quarters by census block

description: The Address Count Listing Files of the U.S. Census Bureau give total housing units (including transitory units) and total group quarters counts for every current census block, drawn from the Master Address File. They are generated twice a year from July and November data and cover all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the Island Areas; the files based on July 2026 data were the latest on 27 September 2026. Two map viewers accompany them: the Address Count Listing Files Viewer for the current release and the Housing Unit Change Viewer, which shows the change in housing units from 2020 to 2026; a 2020 Census edition and viewer also exist. Format and access: pipe-delimited text files by state on the Census Bureau's FTP site, with technical documentation on the file naming and record layout; free and public domain. Caveats: counts are of addresses in the Census Bureau's frame, not occupied dwellings or people; there are no characteristics, and current block codes differ from 2020 block codes for split blocks. Simulation uses: the most up-to-date official block-level count of housing units between censuses, for allocating exposure and customers to network nodes, updating building-stock baselines for hazard studies, and tracking new development in service territories. Related records: the 2020 P.L. 94-171 redistricting data (the 2020 block counts), Population and Housing Unit Estimates, the Building Permits Survey, TIGER/Line blocks, and building footprint datasets such as FEMA USA Structures.
